name: Set the annual investment plan and strategy benchmarks
summary: Each autumn every asset class team writes a plan for the next year: target size from the clients' asset mixes, pacing of private commitments, the split between internal teams and external managers, manager changes and the benchmark and active risk budget for its strategy. Risk researches any benchmark change, finance checks cost, the CIO challenges each plan, the plans are consolidated and checked for liquidity, and the Management Investment Committee recommends the plan and benchmarks to the board for approval. The work is slow because it runs to fixed committee and board dates, waits for the last plan before consolidation, and benchmark changes are contested because they drive measured value added and incentive pay.

baseline.org_archetype: A provincial not-for-profit asset manager of about 240 staff that invests about $79 billion for a few public pension plans and an insurance board through pooled funds and segregated accounts, on a cost recovery basis.
baseline.notes: About nine strategy plans a year (public equities, fixed income, public market alternatives, global credit, private equity, real estate, infrastructure, money market and overlays, plus pooled vehicles). Benchmarks for each asset class strategy were formalised in 2019 and used from January 2020.

trigger: The investment office launches the annual planning cycle after the new capital market assumptions are published, using the board's strategic direction and the latest manager reviews.
end_state: The board has approved the plan and its benchmark and risk budget, teams are notified, and any new benchmark and compliance rule is set up in systems.

volume.seasonality: All plans run between August and December; nothing happens in the first half of the year apart from in-year amendments.

evidence.note: About nine plans a year averaged over twelve months, as in the organisation file.

steps.name: Launch the annual planning cycle
steps.description: The investment office sends each asset class head the plan template and calendar (plans due in September, CIO challenge in October, Management Investment Committee in November, board in December) with the common inputs: the new capital market assumptions, last year's results, the cost budget envelope and changes to client asset mixes.

error.defect_description: An input, such as a client's new asset mix, is missing from the pack.

evidence.note: Annual investment policy statements per asset class and board approval of benchmarks are described; the calendar and times are author estimates.

steps.name: Aggregate client targets into asset class sizes
steps.description: A portfolio construction associate takes each client's approved asset mix and transition path, projected assets and cash flows and converts them into the dollar target for each asset class at the end of next year and over three years, showing how far each class is from target.

error.defect_description: An out-of-date client mix or asset projection is used.

evidence.note: Each client sets its own asset mix; the pension client's 2021 mix is phased in over four years, so targets move each year. Times are author estimates.

steps.name: Review last year's results and set priorities
steps.description: The asset class head reviews the strategy's net value added against its benchmark, risk used, manager reviews and watch list, deal pipeline and team capacity, and drafts the priorities for next year.

error.defect_description: Underperformance is explained away without evidence.

evidence.note: Net value added is measured against each asset class benchmark; plan inputs follow the organisation file. Times are author estimates.

steps.name: Build the commitment pacing model
steps.description: For private equity, real estate, infrastructure and private credit, a principal projects calls, distributions and values of existing commitments with a Takahashi-Alexander style model and solves for next year's commitment budget, number and size of fund commitments and co-investments, split by client account.

error.defect_description: Call and distribution rates are too optimistic, so the plan overshoots or undershoots the target.

evidence.note: Pacing models project calls, distributions and NAV and output an annual commitment budget; overshooting is costly. Times are author estimates.

steps.name: Analyse internal and external management and manager changes
steps.description: For public equities, fixed income, public market alternatives and public credit, a portfolio manager reviews which mandates to bring in house or hand to external managers, which managers to cut or resize on the evidence of manager reviews, fee savings and capacity, and which manager searches the plan needs.

error.defect_description: Fee savings or capacity of internal teams are overstated.

evidence.note: The model manager cut external managers from 200 to 124 and keeps honing its roster to cut fees. Times are author estimates.

steps.name: Draft the asset class plan
steps.description: The asset class head writes the plan: target size, deployment or pacing, internal and external split, manager changes, new pools, headcount and cost, responsible investing items and the proposed benchmark and active risk target, in slides with supporting numbers.

error.defect_description: Plan numbers do not tie to client targets or the cost envelope, or the benchmark proposal is not researched.

evidence.note: Plan contents follow the organisation file's process description and the model manager's investment policy statements. Times are author estimates.

steps.name: Risk reviews the strategy benchmark
steps.description: The director of portfolio risk checks whether the existing benchmark still fits the strategy (investable, matches what the team may buy, set before the period) or whether the team's proposed change deserves full research.

error.defect_description: None introduced; errors pass through.

control.basis: The model manager benchmark policy: the Risk function researches, analyses and reviews strategy benchmarks

evidence.note: The benchmark policy and Risk's role are stated in the 2021 and 2022 annual reports; the share of plans with a change is an author estimate.

steps.name: Research the proposed benchmark change
steps.description: A senior risk manager back-tests candidate indices, compares tracking error, investability, hedged and unhedged versions and licence costs, shows the effect on past net value added and on incentive pay, and writes a benchmark change memo.

error.defect_description: A custom blend or currency hedging basis is specified ambiguously.

evidence.note: Risk is responsible for benchmark research and analysis; content of the memo and times are author estimates.

steps.name: Present the benchmark change to client staff
steps.description: The client relationship manager explains the proposed benchmark change to each affected client's investment staff, because client policies list asset class benchmarks and clients judge results against them.

error.defect_description: None introduced; errors pass through.

evidence.note: Client policies list strategy benchmarks set by the model manager; the consultation step is an author assumption.

steps.name: Clients review the proposed benchmark
steps.description: Client staff, and sometimes their consultant, review the change and reply with questions or agreement, which can take until their own committee meets.

error.defect_description: None introduced; errors pass through.

next.condition: client asks for a different benchmark

evidence.note: Author estimate of client response times.

steps.name: Set the active risk budget
steps.description: The risk manager turns the plan's tracking error target into an active risk budget, adds up the budgets across plans against the total active risk appetite and checks leverage and liquidity effects of the plan.

error.defect_description: Risk budgets across plans add up to more than the total appetite.

evidence.note: The insurance client states that the model manager establishes benchmarks and relative return and risk targets for each strategy; times are author estimates.

steps.name: Finance checks cost and headcount
steps.description: A finance analyst compares the plan's headcount, external manager fees, data and systems costs with the cost budget envelope and flags overruns to the asset class head and the CIO.

error.defect_description: None introduced; errors pass through.

evidence.note: Cost recovery from clients makes budget fit a standard check; times are author estimates.

steps.name: Senior managing director reviews the plan
steps.description: The senior managing director for equities and credit reviews the plans of the teams reporting to him for consistency, capacity and cost before they go to the CIO.

error.defect_description: None introduced; errors pass through.

evidence.note: Reporting lines from the organisation file; times are author estimates.

steps.name: CIO challenge session
steps.description: The chief investment officer, with the heads of total portfolio, risk and finance, challenges each plan in a one to two hour session: size, pacing, internal and external split, risk budget, cost and benchmark.

error.defect_description: None introduced; errors pass through.

control.basis: CIO accountability for the investment plan before Management Investment Committee review

evidence.note: Author estimate based on common practice; the organisation file says the CIO, risk and finance check the plans.

steps.name: Revise the plan
steps.description: The asset class head and team rework the plan for the points raised: smaller or slower deployment, a different manager change, a lower cost or a revised risk budget.

error.defect_description: A change is made in the slides but not in the numbers.

evidence.note: Author estimate.

steps.name: Consolidate plans into the total investment plan
steps.description: The investment office combines the plans, checks that asset class sizes add up to the clients' targets, totals commitments, cost and active risk, and builds the consolidated deck. It waits until the last plan is in.

error.defect_description: A plan's figures are carried into the consolidation incorrectly.

evidence.note: Author estimate; the organisation file says the board approves a consolidated plan.

steps.name: Check consolidated pacing against liquidity
steps.description: A total portfolio manager runs the consolidated commitments and expected calls through each client's liquidity forecast and coverage ratio, and checks overlay and leverage capacity, to make sure no client becomes a forced seller.

error.defect_description: None introduced; errors pass through.

control.basis: Liquidity risk framework: coverage ratio includes capital calls on private market commitments

evidence.note: The liquidity coverage ratio's outflows include capital calls; times are author estimates.

steps.name: Management Investment Committee reviews and recommends
steps.description: The Management Investment Committee, co-chaired by the CIO and chief risk officer with the general counsel, reviews the plan and any benchmark changes and recommends them to the board, or asks for changes.

error.defect_description: None introduced; errors pass through.

control.basis: The model manager benchmark policy and Investment Approval Policy: the Management Investment Committee recommends benchmarks and benchmark changes to the board

evidence.note: Committee composition and its role in recommending benchmarks are stated; times are author estimates.

steps.name: Prepare the board paper
steps.description: The investment office turns the recommended plan and benchmark changes into a board paper with an executive summary and resolution, gets the CIO's sign-off and submits it to the board secretariat by the paper deadline.

error.defect_description: Resolution omits a benchmark effective date.

evidence.note: Author estimate.

steps.name: Board approves the plan and benchmarks
steps.description: The board, through its investment committee of all directors from late 2021, reviews the plan and benchmark changes at its scheduled meeting and approves them or asks for changes.

error.defect_description: None introduced; errors pass through.

control.basis: The model manager benchmark policy: the board approves strategy benchmarks

evidence.note: Board approval of benchmarks is stated; wait reflects the board calendar (author estimate).

steps.name: Publish the approved plan and notify teams
steps.description: The investment office files the approved plan and investment policy statement updates and tells risk, performance, compliance, data management, total portfolio and client relationship teams which benchmarks and risk budgets change and from when.

error.defect_description: None introduced; errors pass through.

next.condition: benchmark or risk budget set-up needed

evidence.note: Author estimate.

steps.name: Set up new benchmarks and risk budgets in systems
steps.description: An investment data analyst sets up the new index or custom blend in the security master and index feeds, and the performance and risk systems, effective from the start of the year, and checks the first calculated values.

error.defect_description: The wrong index variant (hedged or unhedged, gross or net) is loaded.

evidence.note: Author estimate; set-up often waits until year end.

steps.name: Code investment policy statement changes into compliance rules
steps.description: A compliance analyst updates pre-trade and post-trade rules in the order management system for changed permitted investments, limits or ranges in the asset class investment policy statement and tests them.

error.defect_description: A limit is coded with the wrong base or threshold.

control.basis: OSC order on the model manager: compliance system must prevent investments that contravene restrictions in each investment management agreement

evidence.note: The exemption order requires a compliance system that prevents contraventions; times are author estimates.

exceptions.name: Benchmark change proposed
exceptions.description: The team or Risk proposes a new benchmark; Risk researches it and client staff are consulted before the Management Investment Committee recommends it.

exceptions.name: Client objects to a benchmark change
exceptions.description: A client asks for a different benchmark, sending the research back for another option.

exceptions.name: Plan revised after CIO challenge
exceptions.description: The CIO, senior managing director or Management Investment Committee asks for a smaller, slower or cheaper plan.

exceptions.name: Pacing cut for liquidity
exceptions.description: Consolidated commitments would leave a client short of liquid assets under stress, so pacing is reduced.

exceptions.name: Board asks for changes
exceptions.description: Directors ask for changes to a plan or benchmark, delaying approval to a later meeting.

benchmarks.unit: calendar days from launch of the planning cycle to board approval and set-up
benchmarks.population: Asset class plans at a Canadian public-sector asset manager

evidence.note: Author estimate of an August launch and December board approval, with set-up into January for changed benchmarks.

benchmarks.unit: market-based or custom benchmark per asset class investment policy statement
benchmarks.population: The model manager asset class strategies

evidence.note: Stated in the 2021 and 2022 annual reports.

benchmarks.population: The insurance client insurance fund policy asset mix (current)

evidence.note: Current policy; leverage was first used in 2022.

pain_points.description: Benchmark changes are contested because they change measured value added and incentive pay, and they need research, client consultation and two committee approvals.

evidence.note: Benchmark governance runs through Risk, the Management Investment Committee and the board; committees should vote on benchmark changes.

pain_points.description: Commitment pacing depends on uncertain call and distribution rates, so plans overshoot or undershoot private targets.

evidence.note: Pacing models are deterministic and overshooting private targets is costly.

pain_points.description: Consolidation waits for the slowest plan, and the whole cycle is set by fixed committee and board dates.

evidence.note: Author judgement from the step structure.

assumptions: Unit of work is one asset class strategy plan (about nine a year); consolidation, committee and board steps are shared by all plans and their time is counted per plan.

Plan-owner steps are shown under md_private_equity as the representative asset class head; the heads of public equities, fixed income, public market alternatives, global credit, real estate and infrastructure do the same steps for their own plans with the same cost range. principal_private_equity and pm_public_equities likewise stand for the private and public markets staff who build pacing and manager analyses; both are organisation file roles not listed on this process_map entry.
Client consultation on benchmark changes and the compliance coding step are author assumptions; client policies list benchmarks set by the model manager, so changes are explained before approval.
The board approves benchmarks per the model manager's benchmark policy; from September 2021 investment matters went to the Board Investment Committee, which comprises all directors.
No public source gives the model manager's planning calendar or review times; times are author estimates.
Loaded costs are the organisation file's ranges.

sources.title: The model manager 2021 Annual Report
sources.supports: 10 board, 6 finance and audit, 6 human resources and compensation, 4 nominating and governance meetings and 2 Board Investment Committee meetings in 2021; nine directors; Board Investment Committee of all directors created 23 September 2021 to approve investment decisions and review asset allocation advice; four board committees and their mandates; annual board evaluation; Management Investment Committee co-chaired by the CIO and chief risk officer with the general counsel and other senior managers, which must first recommend every investment decision needing board approval; three Investment Department Committees (Total Portfolio, Equities and Credit, Real Assets) set up in 2021 that approve up to thresholds; Investment Approval Policy; one benchmark per asset class investment policy statement; benchmark policy (Risk researches and reviews, Management Investment Committee recommends, board approves); liquidity coverage ratio of high-quality liquid assets to stressed net outflows including client outflows, rebalancing, capital calls and foreign exchange hedging, under past stresses and a one-in-20-year event; counterparty exposure measured daily with ISDA netting and collateral; clean SOC 1 Type I report on control design. Read from a text copy saved under scratch/.

Read from a text copy saved under scratch/ (current policy, after the reference period).

sources.title: The pension client 2021 Annual Report
sources.supports: New strategic asset allocation approved April 2021 and implemented by the model manager over four years, adding portfolio leverage; futures subject to daily cash margining; foreign exchange forwards used for passive and active hedging; currency forwards notional of about $6.5 billion at end 2021, all maturing within one year. Read from a text copy saved under scratch/.

sources.title: The Evolution of the Yale Model for Institutional Investing
sources.supports: Takahashi-Alexander model projects contributions, distributions and NAV per quarter from rate of contribution, commitment, fund life, bow factor, growth and yield; widely used by limited partners; deterministic, so Monte Carlo is suggested.

sources.title: The Private Equity Pacing Model: 3 Key Challenges Investors Face
sources.supports: Pacing models plan cash flows to and from private fund stakes, commonly with the Takahashi-Alexander model; investors must reach targets without overshooting because selling stakes is costly; scaling to target takes years.

sources.title: Commitment Pacing (glossary)
sources.supports: A pacing model projects calls, distributions and NAV for every existing commitment and outputs an annual commitment budget split across strategies; run annually or quarterly; built with consultants or internal quantitative teams.

sources.title: Endowment Governance Part 3: Process and Engagement
sources.supports: Chair owns the agenda with staff; materials at least a week before the meeting; regular meetings of two to four hours; record attendance, votes by name and recusals; circulate minutes promptly to confirm decisions; members should vote on asset allocation, benchmark and risk parameter changes.

sources.title: The model manager, Commission and Director decisions (exemptions for the model manager and its investment pools)
sources.supports: Compliance system must prevent investments that contravene restrictions set out in each investment management agreement; fairness in allocating investment opportunities among members and pools; commodity futures advising rules. Read from a text copy saved under scratch/.
